availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

<file name="frontend/app.js" language="javascript" >
<content>
'use strict';

const $ = (id) => document.getElementById(id);
const fields = ['unit_id', 'function_code', 'address', 'quantity', 'scale'];
const categories = [
  ['observations', 'Observations'],
  ['possible_causes', 'Possible causes'],
  ['training_hints', 'Training hints'],
  ['next_steps', 'Next steps'],
];
let scenarios = [];
let history = [];
const caseHistory = new Map();
let running = false;

function text(value, fallback = 'Not returned') {
  if (value === null || value === undefined || value === '') return fallback;
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.length ? value.map((item) => text(item)).join(', ') : fallback;
  if (typeof value === 'object') return JSON.stringify(value);
  return String(value);
}
function engineeringValue(result) {
  const value = result.engineering_value;
  if (value === null || value === undefined || value === '') return 'Not returned';
  return `${text(value)}${result.unit ? ` ${text(result.unit)}` : ''}`;
}

function validateScale() {
  const input = $('scale');
  input.setCustomValidity(input.value !== '' && Number(input.value) <= 0 ? 'Scale must be greater than zero.' : '');
}

function verifiedText(value) {
  if (value === true) return 'Verified by this simulated test.';
  if (value === false) return 'Not verified by this simulated test.';
  return text(value, 'No verification result returned.');
}

function sourceText(value) {
  if (value === 'openai-compatible') return 'Source: AI provider';
  if (value === 'deterministic') return 'Source: deterministic fallback';
  return `Source: ${text(value, 'not specified')}`;
}

function fillList(element, values) {
  element.replaceChildren();
  const items = Array.isArray(values) ? values : (values == null ? [] : [values]);
  for (const item of items.length ? items : ['None returned.']) {
    const li = document.createElement('li');
    li.textContent = text(item);
    element.append(li);
  }
}

function addText(parent, tag, value, className) {
  const node = document.createElement(tag);
  node.textContent = value;
  if (className) node.className = className;
  parent.append(node);
  return node;
}

function renderDocumentation(documentation) {
  const container = $('documentation');
  container.replaceChildren();
  const entries = Array.isArray(documentation) ? documentation : [documentation];
  for (const entry of entries) addText(container, 'p', text(entry, 'No documentation returned.'));
}

function selectScenario() {
  const scenario = scenarios.find((item) => item.id === $('scenario').value);
  if (!scenario) return;
  $('scenario-summary').textContent = text(scenario.summary, '');
  renderDocumentation(scenario.documentation);
  $('history-scenario').textContent = `Scenario: ${text(scenario.title)}`;
  history = caseHistory.get(scenario.id) || [];
  const latest = history[history.length - 1];
  for (const field of fields) $(field).value = latest?.request?.[field] ?? scenario.initial[field];
  validateScale();
  if (latest) {
    renderResult(latest);
  } else {
    $('result').hidden = true;
    $('empty-result').hidden = false;
    $('result-status').textContent = 'Awaiting read';
    $('result-status').dataset.state = '';
  }
  $('test-message').dataset.state = '';
  $('test-message').textContent = '';
  $('run-test').textContent = latest ? 'Retest simulated read' : 'Run simulated read';
  renderHistory();
  const security = scenario.category === 'security';
  $('incident-panel').hidden = !security;
  if (security) showIncident(scenario);
}

async function api(path, options) {
  const response = await fetch(path, options);
  let data;
  try { data = await response.json(); } catch { throw new Error(`Server returned an unreadable response (HTTP ${response.status}).`); }
  if (!response.ok) {
    const detail = data.detail || data.error || data.message;
    throw new Error(detail ? text(detail) : `Request failed (HTTP ${response.status}).`);
  }
  return data;
}

async function loadScenarios() {
  $('load-message').hidden = false;
  $('load-message').textContent = 'Loading scenarios…';
  $('load-message').dataset.state = '';
  $('retry-load').hidden = true;
  $('setup-content').hidden = true;
  try {
    const data = await api('/api/scenarios');
    if (!Array.isArray(data.scenarios) || !data.scenarios.length) throw new Error('No scenarios were returned.');
    scenarios = data.scenarios;
    $('scenario').replaceChildren();
    const groups = [['troubleshooting', 'Troubleshooting'], ['security', 'Security incidents']];
    for (const [category, label] of groups) {
      const members = scenarios.filter((scenario) => scenario.category === category);
      if (!members.length) continue;
      const group = document.createElement('optgroup');
      group.label = label;
      for (const scenario of members) {
        const option = document.createElement('option');
        option.value = scenario.id;
        option.textContent = scenario.difficulty ? `${text(scenario.title)} · ${text(scenario.difficulty)}` : text(scenario.title);
        group.append(option);
      }
      $('scenario').append(group);
    }
    for (const scenario of scenarios.filter((item) => !groups.some(([category]) => category === item.category))) {
      const option = document.createElement('option');
      option.value = scenario.id;
      option.textContent = text(scenario.title);
      $('scenario').append(option);
    }
    selectScenario();
    $('setup-content').hidden = false;
    $('load-message').hidden = true;
  } catch (error) {
    $('load-message').textContent = `Could not load scenarios: ${error.message}`;
    $('load-message').dataset.state = 'error';
    $('retry-load').hidden = false;
  }
}

function renderResult(result) {
  $('empty-result').hidden = true;
  $('result').hidden = false;
  $('result-status').textContent = `Status: ${text(result.status, 'unknown')}`;
  $('result-status').dataset.state = result.status === 'response' ? 'success' : (result.status === 'exception' || result.status === 'error' ? 'error' : '');
  $('engineering-value').textContent = engineeringValue(result);
  $('raw-registers').textContent = text(result.raw_registers);
  for (const [key] of categories) fillList($(key), result[key]);
  $('verified').textContent = verifiedText(result.verified);
  $('verified').parentElement.dataset.state = result.verified === true ? 'success' : '';
  $('explanation').textContent = text(result.explanation, 'No explanation returned.');
  $('explanation-source').textContent = sourceText(result.explanation_source);
  renderFrames($('frames'), result.frames, 'read');
}

let frameIds = 0;
// Renders frames returned by the server. Every byte and value comes from the response; textContent only.
function renderFrames(container, frames, label) {
  container.replaceChildren();
  if (!Array.isArray(frames) || !frames.length) {
    addText(container, 'p', 'No frame was returned: the request bytes did not reach the simulator.', 'muted');
    return;
  }
  for (const frame of frames) {
    const id = `frame-${label}-${++frameIds}`;
    const block = document.createElement('section');
    block.className = 'frame';
    block.setAttribute('aria-labelledby', `${id}-title`);
    const heading = addText(block, 'h4', frame.direction === 'request' ? 'Request sent to simulator' : 'Response from simulator');
    heading.id = `${id}-title`;
    const hex = document.createElement('code');
    hex.className = 'hex';
    hex.setAttribute('aria-label', `${heading.textContent}, hexadecimal bytes`);
    const bytes = text(frame.hex, '').split(' ').filter(Boolean);
    bytes.forEach((byte, index) => {
      if (index) hex.append(' ');
      const span = document.createElement('span');
      span.dataset.i = String(index);
      span.textContent = byte;
      hex.append(span);
    });
    block.append(hex);
    const table = document.createElement('table');
    table.className = 'frame-table';
    const caption = addText(table, 'caption', `${heading.textContent}: decoded fields (simulated)`);
    caption.className = 'visually-hidden';
    const head = document.createElement('thead');
    const headRow = document.createElement('tr');
    for (const name of ['Field', 'Bytes (hex)', 'Decoded value']) {
      const th = addText(headRow, 'th', name);
      th.scope = 'col';
    }
    head.append(headRow);
    table.append(head);
    const body = document.createElement('tbody');
    const spans = Array.from(hex.querySelectorAll('span'));
    (Array.isArray(frame.fields) ? frame.fields : []).forEach((field, index) => {
      const offset = Number(field?.bytes?.offset);
      const length = Number(field?.bytes?.length);
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      row.tabIndex = 0;
      const nameCell = addText(row, 'th', text(field.name));
      nameCell.scope = 'row';
      const bytesCell = document.createElement('td');
      addText(bytesCell, 'code', bytes.slice(offset, offset + length).join(' '));
      const range = addText(bytesCell, 'span', length > 1 ? ` bytes ${offset}–${offset + length - 1}` : ` byte ${offset}`, 'range');
      range.id = `${id}-range-${index}`;
      row.setAttribute('aria-describedby', range.id);
      row.append(bytesCell);
      addText(row, 'td', text(field.value));
      const highlight = (on) => {
        spans.forEach((span, i) => span.classList.toggle('hl', on && i >= offset && i < offset + length));
        row.classList.toggle('active', on);
      };
      row.addEventListener('mouseenter', () => highlight(true));
      row.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => highlight(false));
      row.addEventListener('focusin', () => highlight(true));
      row.addEventListener('focusout', () => highlight(false));
      body.append(row);
    });
    if (frame.decode_error) {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      row.className = 'decode-error';
      const cell = addText(row, 'td', `Decode error: ${text(frame.decode_error)}`);
      cell.colSpan = 3;
      body.append(row);
    }
    table.append(body);
    block.append(table);
    container.append(block);
  }
}
function renderComparison() {
  const container = $('comparison-results');
  container.replaceChildren();
  const hasComparison = history.length >= 2;
  $('comparison-empty').hidden = hasComparison;
  container.hidden = !hasComparison;
  if (!hasComparison) return;

  const previous = history[history.length - 2];
  const current = history[history.length - 1];
  for (const [label, entry, number] of [
    ['Previous', previous, history.length - 1],
    ['Current', current, history.length],
  ]) {
    const section = document.createElement('section');
    section.className = 'comparison-read';
    addText(section, 'h3', `${label} · read ${number}`);
    const request = entry.request || {};
    addText(section, 'p', `Request: unit ${text(request.unit_id)}, function ${text(request.function_code)}, address ${text(request.address)}, quantity ${text(request.quantity)}, scale ${text(request.scale)}.`);
    addText(section, 'p', `Status: ${text(entry.status, 'unknown')}. Raw registers: ${text(entry.raw_registers)}. Engineering value: ${engineeringValue(entry)} (simulated).`);
    addText(section, 'p', verifiedText(entry.verified));
    container.append(section);
  }
  const changed = fields.filter((field) => previous.request?.[field] !== current.request?.[field]);
  const labels = { unit_id: 'Unit ID', function_code: 'Function code', address: 'Address', quantity: 'Quantity', scale: 'Scale' };
  addText(container, 'p', changed.length
    ? `Changed settings: ${changed.map((field) => `${labels[field]} (${text(previous.request?.[field])} to ${text(current.request?.[field])})`).join(', ')}.`
    : 'No request settings changed between these reads.', 'comparison-changes');
}


function renderHistory() {
  const list = $('history-list');
  list.replaceChildren();
  $('history-empty').hidden = history.length > 0;
  $('print-report').disabled = history.length === 0;
  renderComparison();
  history.forEach((entry, index) => {
    const item = document.createElement('li');
    const details = document.createElement('details');
    const summary = document.createElement('summary');
    summary.textContent = `Read ${index + 1} · ${text(entry.status, 'unknown')} · ${verifiedText(entry.verified)}`;
    details.append(summary);
    const body = document.createElement('div');
    body.className = 'history-detail';
    const request = entry.request || {};
    addText(body, 'p', `Request: unit ${text(request.unit_id)}, function ${text(request.function_code)}, address ${text(request.address)}, quantity ${text(request.quantity)}, scale ${text(request.scale)}.`);
    addText(body, 'p', `Raw registers: ${text(entry.raw_registers)}. Engineering value: ${engineeringValue(entry)} (simulated).`);
    for (const frame of Array.isArray(entry.frames) ? entry.frames : []) {
      addText(body, 'p', `${frame.direction === 'request' ? 'Request frame' : 'Response frame'} (simulated, hex): ${text(frame.hex)}${frame.decode_error ? ` · Decode error: ${text(frame.decode_error)}` : ''}`, 'hex-line');
    }
    for (const [key, label] of categories) {
      addText(body, 'h3', label);
      const ul = document.createElement('ul');
      fillList(ul, entry[key]);
      body.append(ul);
    }
    addText(body, 'h3', `Explanation · ${sourceText(entry.explanation_source)}`);
    addText(body, 'p', text(entry.explanation, 'No explanation returned.'));
    details.append(body);
    item.append(details);
    list.append(item);
  });

// ---- Security incident: simulated traffic log and answer ----
const incidentLogs = new Map();
const answerHistory = new Map();
const verifiedTransaction = new Map();
let answering = false;

function currentScenario() { return scenarios.find((item) => item.id === $('scenario').value); }

async function showIncident(scenario) {
  $('answer-result').hidden = true;
  const attempts = answerHistory.get(scenario.id) || [];
  if (attempts.length) renderAnswer(attempts[attempts.length - 1]);
  if (incidentLogs.has(scenario.id)) { renderLog(scenario.id); return; }
  $('log-body').replaceChildren();
  $('log-note').textContent = 'Loading the simulated capture…';
  try {
    const log = await api(`/api/incident/${encodeURIComponent(scenario.id)}/log`);
    incidentLogs.set(scenario.id, log);
    if (currentScenario()?.id === scenario.id) renderLog(scenario.id);
  } catch (error) {
    $('log-note').textContent = `Could not load the simulated traffic log: ${error.message}`;
  }
}

function renderLog(scenarioId) {
  const log = incidentLogs.get(scenarioId);
  const body = $('log-body');
  body.replaceChildren();
  $('log-note').textContent = `Simulated capture. ${text(log.capture_note, '')}`;
  const flagged = verifiedTransaction.get(scenarioId);
  for (const entry of Array.isArray(log.entries) ? log.entries : []) {
    const row = document.createElement('tr');
    const seq = addText(row, 'td', text(entry.sequence));

      row.setAttribute('aria-label', `Sequence ${text(entry.sequence)}: unauthorized write, verified by your answer`);
      seq.append(document.createElement('br'));
      addText(seq, 'strong', '⚠ Unauthorized write', 'flag');

    addText(row, 'td', text(entry.client));
    addText(row, 'td', text(entry.transaction_id));
    addText(row, 'td', text(entry.unit_id));
    addText(row, 'td', `${String(entry.function_code).padStart(2, '0')} · ${text(entry.function_name)}`);
    addText(row, 'td', text(entry.address));
    addText(row, 'td', text(entry.values));
    const framesCell = document.createElement('td');
    const details = document.createElement('details');
    addText(details, 'summary', `Frames for transaction ${text(entry.transaction_id)}`);
    const frames = document.createElement('div');
    details.append(frames);
    details.addEventListener('toggle', () => { if (details.open && !frames.childElementCount) renderFrames(frames, entry.frames, `log-${entry.sequence}`); });
    framesCell.append(details);
    row.append(framesCell);

    });
    row.append(actionCell);
    body.append(row);
  }
}

function renderAnswer(result) {
  $('answer-result').hidden = false;
  const ok = result.verified === true;
  $('answer-status').textContent = ok ? 'Status: answer verified' : 'Status: answer not verified';
  $('answer-status').dataset.state = ok ? 'success' : 'error';
  for (const key of ['observations', 'possible_causes', 'training_hints', 'next_steps']) fillList($(`answer-${key}`), result[key]);
  const mitigations = Array.isArray(result.mitigations) ? result.mitigations : [];

}

function renderAnswerHistory() {

$('answer-form').addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {

function text(value, fallback = 'Not returned') {
  if (value === null || value === undefined || value === '') return fallback;

  if (typeof value === 'object') return JSON.stringify(value);

}

  if (value === null || value === undefined || value === '') return 'Not returned';

function validateScale() {
  const input = $('scale');

function verifiedText(value) {
  if (value === true) return 'Verified by this simulated test.';
  if (value === false) return 'Not verified by this simulated test.';
  return text(value, 'No verification result returned.');
}

function sourceText(value) {
  if (value === 'openai-compatible') return 'Source: AI provider';
  if (value === 'deterministic') return 'Source: deterministic fallback';
  return `Source: ${text(value, 'not specified')}`;
}

function fillList(element, values) {
  element.replaceChildren();
  const items = Array.isArray(values) ? values : (values == null ? [] : [values]);

    addText(row, 'td', text(entry.unit_id));
    addText(row, 'td', `${String(entry.function_code).padStart(2, '0')} · ${text(entry.function_name)}`);
    addText(row, 'td', text(entry.address));
    addText(row, 'td', text(entry.values));
    const framesCell = document.createElement('td');
    const details = document.createElement('details');
    addText(details, 'summary', `Frames for transaction ${text(entry.transaction_id)}`);
    const frames = document.createElement('div');
    details.append(frames);
    details.addEventListener('toggle', () => { if (details.open && !frames.childElementCount) renderFrames(frames, entry.frames, `log-${entry.sequence}`); });
    framesCell.append(details);
    row.append(framesCell);
    const actionCell = document.createElement('td');
    const select = addText(actionCell, 'button', 'Select');
    select.type = 'button';
    select.className = 'secondary';
    select.setAttribute('aria-label', `Select transaction ${text(entry.transaction_id)} from ${text(entry.client)} for your answer`);
    select.addEventListener('click', () => {
      $('answer-transaction').value = entry.transaction_id;
      $('answer-client').value = entry.client;
      $('log-message').textContent = `Transaction ${text(entry.transaction_id)} from ${text(entry.client)} copied into the answer form.`;
    });
    row.append(actionCell);
    body.append(row);
  }
}

function renderAnswer(result) {
  $('answer-result').hidden = false;
  const ok = result.verified === true;
  $('answer-status').textContent = ok ? 'Status: answer verified' : 'Status: answer not verified';
  $('answer-status').dataset.state = ok ? 'success' : 'error';
  for (const key of ['observations', 'possible_causes', 'training_hints', 'next_steps']) fillList($(`answer-${key}`), result[key]);
  const mitigations = Array.isArray(result.mitigations) ? result.mitigations : [];
  $('mitigations-section').hidden = mitigations.length === 0;
  fillList($('answer-mitigations'), mitigations);
  $('answer-verified').textContent = ok ? 'Verified by the simulated capture: this transaction ID and client label match the write.' : 'Not verified by the simulated capture.';
  $('answer-verified').parentElement.dataset.state = ok ? 'success' : '';
  $('answer-explanation').textContent = text(result.explanation, 'No explanation returned.');
  $('answer-explanation-source').textContent = sourceText(result.explanation_source);
}

function renderAnswerHistory() {
  const list = $('answer-history');
  list.replaceChildren();
  const scenario = currentScenario();
  const attempts = scenario ? (answerHistory.get(scenario.id) || []) : [];
  $('answer-history-title').hidden = attempts.length === 0;
  attempts.forEach((entry, index) => {
    const item = document.createElement('li');
    const details = document.createElement('details');
    addText(details, 'summary', `Answer ${index + 1} · transaction ${text(entry.answer?.transaction_id)} · client ${text(entry.answer?.client)} · ${entry.verified === true ? 'Verified by the simulated capture.' : 'Not verified by the simulated capture.'}`);
    const body = document.createElement('div');
    body.className = 'history-detail';
    for (const [key, label] of [...categories, ['mitigations', 'Next steps · real-world guidance, not verified by this simulation']]) {
      if (key === 'mitigations' && !(entry.mitigations || []).length) continue;
      addText(body, 'h3', label);
      const ul = document.createElement('ul');
      fillList(ul, entry[key]);
      body.append(ul);
    }
    addText(body, 'h3', `Explanation · ${sourceText(entry.explanation_source)}`);
    addText(body, 'p', text(entry.explanation, 'No explanation returned.'));
    details.append(body);
    item.append(details);
    list.append(item);
  });
  if (attempts.length) {
    $('print-report').disabled = false;
    $('history-empty').hidden = true;
  }
}

$('answer-form').addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  if (answering) return;
  if (!$('answer-form').reportValidity()) return;
  const scenario = currentScenario();
  if (!scenario || scenario.category !== 'security') return;
  const request = { scenario_id: scenario.id, transaction_id: Number($('answer-transaction').value), client: $('answer-client').value.trim() };
  answering = true;
  $('answer-fields').disabled = true;
  // Not `disabled`: a disabled button would drop keyboard focus while the result is announced.
  $('submit-answer').setAttribute('aria-disabled', 'true');
  $('test-message').dataset.state = '';
  $('test-message').textContent = 'Checking your answer against the simulated capture…';
  try {
    const result = await api('/api/incident/answer', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(request) });
    if (!result.answer) result.answer = request;
    const attempts = answerHistory.get(scenario.id) || [];
    attempts.push(result);
    answerHistory.set(scenario.id, attempts);
    if (result.verified === true) verifiedTransaction.set(scenario.id, result.answer.transaction_id);
    renderAnswer(result);
    if (incidentLogs.has(scenario.id)) renderLog(scenario.id);
    renderAnswerHistory();
    $('test-message').textContent = result.verified === true
      ? 'Answer verified by the simulated capture. The matching log row is now marked "Unauthorized write".'
      : 'Answer not verified by the simulated capture. Review the log and try again.';
  } catch (error) {
    $('test-message').textContent = `Answer failed: ${error.message}`;
    $('test-message').dataset.state = 'error';
  } finally {
    answering = false;
    $('answer-fields').disabled = false;
    $('submit-answer').removeAttribute('aria-disabled');
  }
});

$('scenario').addEventListener('change', selectScenario);
$('scale').addEventListener('input', validateScale);
$('retry-load').addEventListener('click', loadScenarios);
$('print-report').addEventListener('click', () => window.print());
$('test-form').addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  if (running) return;
  validateScale();
  if (!$('test-form').reportValidity()) return;
  const request = { scenario_id: $('scenario').value };
  for (const field of fields) request[field] = Number($(field).value);
  running = true;
  $('scenario').disabled = true;
  $('request-fields').disabled = true;
  $('run-test').disabled = true;
  $('test-message').textContent = 'Reading the local simulator…';
  $('test-message').dataset.state = '';
  try {
    const result = await api('/api/test', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(request) });
    if (!result.request) result.request = request;
    history.push(result);
    caseHistory.set(request.scenario_id, history);
    renderResult(result);
    renderHistory();
    $('run-test').textContent = 'Retest simulated read';
    $('test-message').textContent = 'Read complete. Adjust a setting and retest to compare results.';
  } catch (error) {
    $('test-message').textContent = `Read failed: ${error.message} Check the request and try again.`;
    $('test-message').dataset.state = 'error';
  } finally {
    running = false;
    $('scenario').disabled = false;
    $('request-fields').disabled = false;
    $('run-test').disabled = false;
  }
});

loadScenarios();

</content>
</file>

:root {
  color-scheme: dark;
  --ink: #f2eee6;
  --muted: #c2c3bb;
  --paper: #111516;
  --surface: #202526;
  --line: #6d7976;
  --forest: #ffad69;
  --forest-dark: #11191a;
  --accent: #ffad69;
  --soft: #303839;
  --focus: #ffbc80;
  --success: #92e2a9;
  --error: #ffacaa;
  font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif;
  color: var(--ink);
  background: var(--paper);
  line-height: 1.5;
}
* { box-sizing: border-box; }
[hidden] { display: none !important; }
body { margin: 0; }
button, input, select { font: inherit; }
button, select, summary { cursor: pointer; }
:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 3px; }
.skip-link { position: absolute; left: 1rem; top: -5rem; z-index: 10; padding: .75rem 1rem; background: var(--surface); color: var(--ink); }
.skip-link:focus { top: 1rem; }
.masthead { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; gap: .75rem 1.5rem; padding: 1rem clamp(1rem, 4vw, 4rem); color: white; background: var(--forest-dark); }
.brand { font-size: 1.15rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: -.04em; }
.brand span { font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0; color: var(--muted); }
.safety-label { font-size: .7rem; font-weight: 750; letter-spacing: .08em; }
.safety-label span, footer span { padding: 0 .3rem; }
.page { max-width: 100rem; margin: auto; padding: 2rem 1rem 4rem; }
.intro { display: grid; gap: 1.25rem; margin-bottom: 2rem; }
.eyebrow { margin: 0 0 .5rem; color: var(--forest); font-size: .7rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: .12em; }
h1, h2, h3, p { margin-top: 0; }
h1 { margin-bottom: .5rem; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 750; font-size: clamp(2.25rem, 4.5vw, 4.25rem); line-height: 1.06; letter-spacing: -.04em; }
h2 { margin-bottom: 0; font-size: 1.35rem; line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: -.02em; }
h3 { margin-bottom: .5rem; font-size: .95rem; }
.lede { color: var(--muted); margin-bottom: 0; max-width: 40rem; }
.scope-note { margin: 0; padding: 1rem; border: 1px solid var(--line); font-size: .85rem; color: var(--muted); }
.scope-note strong { color: var(--ink); }
.workflow { margin: 0 0 1.5rem; border-block: 1px solid var(--line); }
.workflow ol { display: grid; gap: .75rem; margin: 0; padding: 1rem 0; list-style: none; counter-reset: workflow; }
.workflow li { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 2rem 1fr; column-gap: .5rem; padding: 0; counter-increment: workflow; }
.workflow li + li { margin: 0; }
.workflow li::before { grid-row: span 2; color: var(--accent); font-weight: 800; content: counter(workflow, decimal-leading-zero); }
.workflow strong { line-height: 1.3; }
.workflow span { color: var(--muted); font-size: .8rem; }
.layout { display: grid; gap: 1rem; align-items: start; }
.results-column { display: grid; gap: 1rem; min-width: 0; }
.panel { min-width: 0; padding: 1.25rem; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); }
.section-heading { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: .75rem 1rem; justify-content: space-between; align-items: start; margin-bottom: 1rem; }
.muted { color: var(--muted); font-size: .875rem; }
label, legend { display: block; color: var(--ink); font-size: .85rem; font-weight: 700; margin-bottom: .4rem; }
select, input { width: 100%; min-width: 0; min-height: 2.75rem; border: 1px solid #a0aaa4; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--paper); color: var(--ink); padding: .55rem .65rem; }
.scenario-summary { color: var(--muted); font-size: .875rem; margin: .65rem 0 1.25rem; }
.documentation { background: var(--soft); padding: .75rem 1rem; margin-bottom: 1.5rem; }
summary { min-height: 2.75rem; font-weight: 700; padding: .65rem 0; }
.doc-content { color: var(--ink); font-size: .875rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.doc-content p:last-child { margin-bottom: .25rem; }
fieldset { border: 0; padding: 0; margin: 0 0 1.25rem; min-width: 0; }
legend { padding: 0; margin-bottom: .85rem; font-size: 1rem; }
.fields { display: grid; gap: 1rem; }
.field-help { color: var(--muted); margin: .4rem 0 0; font-size: .8rem; }
button { min-height: 2.75rem; padding: .7rem 1rem; font-weight: 700; border-radius: 2px; }
button:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: .6; }
.primary { width: 100%; border: 1px solid var(--accent); color: #1c120b; background: var(--accent); }
.primary:hover:not(:disabled) { background: #ffd1a8; }
.secondary { border: 1px solid var(--forest); color: var(--forest); background: transparent; }
.secondary:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--soft); }
.form-message, .notice { font-size: .875rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.form-message:not(:empty) { margin: .75rem 0 0; }
.notice { padding: .75rem; background: var(--soft); margin-bottom: .75rem; }
.status, .source { color: var(--forest); background: var(--soft); padding: .35rem .6rem; font-size: .75rem; font-weight: 700; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.status[data-state="success"], .verification[data-state="success"] .reading-label { color: var(--success); }
.status[data-state="error"], .form-message[data-state="error"], .notice[data-state="error"] { color: var(--error); }
.empty-state { border: 1px dashed var(--line); padding: 2.5rem 1rem; text-align: center; color: var(--muted); }
.empty-state strong { color: var(--ink); }
.empty-state p { margin: .4rem auto 0; max-width: 28rem; }
.reading { display: grid; gap: 1.25rem; padding: 1.25rem; color: var(--ink); background: var(--forest-dark); border: 1px solid var(--line); }
.reading-label { display: block; font-size: .68rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: .1em; }
.reading strong { display: block; font-size: clamp(1.65rem, 3vw, 2.4rem); line-height: 1.2; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.reading-caption { font-size: .8rem; color: var(--muted); }
.raw-reading strong { margin-top: .4rem; font-size: 1.1rem; }
.evidence-grid { display: grid; gap: 1.25rem; margin: 1.5rem 0; }
.evidence-grid section { min-width: 0; }
.evidence-grid h3 span { display: block; margin-top: .2rem; color: var(--muted); font-size: .75rem; font-weight: 500; }
ul { padding-left: 1.2rem; margin: 0; }
li { padding-left: .1rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
li + li { margin-top: .4rem; }
.evidence-grid ul, .history-detail { font-size: .875rem; }
.verification { border-top: 1px solid var(--line); padding: 1rem 0; }
.verification .reading-label { color: var(--forest); }
.verification p { margin: .35rem 0 0; }
.explanation { background: var(--paper); padding: 1rem; }
.explanation-heading { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: start; justify-content: space-between; gap: .5rem; }
.explanation p { margin: .5rem 0 0; white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.comparison-results { display: grid; gap: 1rem; }
.comparison-read { min-width: 0; padding: 1rem; background: var(--paper); border: 1px solid var(--line); }
.comparison-read h3 { color: var(--forest); }
.comparison-read p { margin: .5rem 0 0; font-size: .875rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.comparison-changes { margin: 0; font-size: .875rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.history-list { padding: 0; margin: 0; list-style: none; counter-reset: none; }
.history-list > li { padding: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); }
.history-list > li + li { margin-top: 0; }
.history-list summary { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.history-detail { padding: .25rem 0 1rem; color: var(--muted); }
.history-detail h3 { margin: 1rem 0 .3rem; color: var(--ink); }
.history-detail p:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; white-space: pre-wrap; }
.empty-history { color: var(--muted); font-size: .875rem; margin-bottom: 0; }
footer { padding: 1.25rem 1rem; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); color: var(--muted); font-size: .8rem; text-align: center; }
.visually-hidden { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; border: 0; }
.wire { margin: 0 0 1.25rem; padding: .25rem 1rem .75rem; background: var(--paper); border: 1px solid var(--line); }
.wire-intro p, .terms { font-size: .85rem; color: var(--muted); }
.terms { display: grid; grid-template-columns: max-content 1fr; gap: .25rem .75rem; margin: 0 0 1rem; }
.terms dt { color: var(--ink); font-weight: 700; }
.terms dd { margin: 0; }
.frame { margin-top: 1rem; min-width: 0; }
.frame h4 { margin: 0 0 .4rem; font-size: .9rem; }
.hex, .frame-table code, .hex-line { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace; }
.hex { display: block; padding: .5rem .65rem; background: var(--forest-dark); border: 1px solid var(--line); overflow-wrap: anywhere; font-size: .9rem; }
.hex span { padding: 0 .05rem; transition: background-color .15s ease; }
.hex span.hl { background: var(--accent); color: #1c120b; text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-thickness: 2px; text-underline-offset: 3px; }
.frame-table, .log-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; margin-top: .5rem; font-size: .85rem; }
.frame-table th, .frame-table td, .log-table th, .log-table td { padding: .4rem .5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); text-align: left; vertical-align: top; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.frame-table thead th, .log-table thead th { color: var(--muted); font-size: .75rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: .04em; }
.frame-table tbody tr:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: -3px; }
.frame-table tbody tr.active { background: var(--soft); }
.frame-table .range { color: var(--muted); font-size: .75rem; }
.decode-error td { color: var(--error); font-weight: 700; }
.incident .notice { color: var(--ink); }
.table-scroll { overflow-x: auto; margin-bottom: 1.25rem; }
.log-table caption { text-align: left; color: var(--muted); font-size: .8rem; padding-bottom: .4rem; }
.log-table details summary { min-height: 2.25rem; padding: .3rem 0; font-weight: 600; }
.log-table button { min-height: 2.25rem; padding: .35rem .7rem; }
.log-table tr[data-flag="unauthorized"] { background: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, transparent 0 8px, rgba(255, 172, 170, .12) 8px 16px); }
.log-table tr[data-flag="unauthorized"] > :first-child { border-left: 6px double var(--error); }
.log-table tr[data-flag="unauthorized"]:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: -3px; }
.flag { display: inline-block; margin-top: .25rem; padding: .1rem .4rem; border: 1px dashed var(--error); color: var(--error); font-weight: 800; font-size: .75rem; }
.answer-form { margin-bottom: 1.25rem; }
.answer-result { border-top: 1px solid var(--line); padding-top: 1rem; }
.answer-result .status { display: inline-block; margin-bottom: .5rem; }
.mitigations { margin-bottom: 1rem; }
.mitigations ul { font-size: .875rem; }
.answer-history-title { margin: 1.25rem 0 .5rem; }
.hex-line { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after { transition: none !important; animation: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; }
}
@media (min-width: 36rem) {
  .page { padding-inline: 2rem; }
  .fields, .evidence-grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); }
  .field-wide { grid-column: 1 / -1; }
  .workflow ol { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); }
  .comparison-results { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); }
  .comparison-changes { grid-column: 1 / -1; }
  .reading { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; }
  .panel { padding: 1.5rem; }
}
@media (min-width: 58rem) {
  .page { padding-inline: clamp(2rem, 4vw, 4rem); }
  .intro { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(15rem, 22rem); align-items: end; }
  .workflow ol { grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr)); }
  .layout { grid-template-columns: minmax(19rem, 24rem) minmax(0, 1fr); }
}
@media print {
  :root { color-scheme: light; --ink: #111; --muted: #333; --paper: white; --surface: white; --line: #555; --forest: #111; --forest-dark: white; --soft: white; --success: #111; --error: #111; color: black; background: white; }
  .skip-link, button, .workflow, .setup, .evidence, .incident { display: none !important; }
  .page { max-width: none; padding: 0; }
  .layout, .intro { display: block; }
  .panel, .scope-note { border: 0; padding: .5rem 0; break-inside: avoid; }
  .masthead, .reading { color: black; background: white; border-bottom: 1px solid black; }
  .reading-caption { color: black; }
  .history-list details > * { display: block; }
  .history-list li { break-inside: avoid; }
  .hex, .hex span.hl { background: white; color: black; text-decoration: none; }
  .hex-line { font-size: .8rem; }
}

</content>
</file>

using System.Net;
using System.Text.Json;
using System.Threading.RateLimiting;
using GhostWire;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting;
using Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders;

var app = GhostWireHost.Create(args);
await app.RunAsync();

namespace GhostWire
{
    public static class GhostWireHost
    {
        public static WebApplication Create(string[] args, int? port = null)
        {
            int selectedPort = port ?? PortFromEnvironment();
            var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(new WebApplicationOptions { Args = args, ContentRootPath = AppContext.BaseDirectory });
            builder.WebHost.ConfigureKestrel(options =>
            {
                options.Listen(IPAddress.Loopback, selectedPort);
                options.Limits.MaxRequestBodySize = 16384;
                options.Limits.MaxConcurrentConnections = 64;
                options.Limits.RequestHeadersTimeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10);
            });
            builder.Services.AddSingleton<TrainingService>();
            builder.Services.AddRateLimiter(options =>
            {
                options.RejectionStatusCode = StatusCodes.Status429TooManyRequests;
                options.GlobalLimiter = PartitionedRateLimiter.Create<HttpContext, string>(context =>
                    RateLimitPartition.GetFixedWindowLimiter("local", _ => new FixedWindowRateLimiterOptions
                    {
                        PermitLimit = 120, Window = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1), QueueLimit = 0, AutoReplenishment = true
                    }));
            });
            var app = builder.Build();
            // Resolve eagerly so a Phantom Writer generation failure stops startup instead of failing the first request.
            app.Services.GetRequiredService<TrainingService>();
            var concurrentTests = new SemaphoreSlim(8);
            app.Use(async (context, next) =>
            {
                var host = context.Request.Host;
                bool validHost = (string.Equals(host.Host, "localhost", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) || host.Host == "127.0.0.1") && host.Port == context.Connection.LocalPort;
                bool local = context.Connection.RemoteIpAddress != null && IPAddress.IsLoopback(context.Connection.RemoteIpAddress);
                if (!validHost || !local)
                {
                    context.Response.StatusCode = 403;
                    await context.Response.WriteAsJsonAsync(new { error = "Forbidden host" });
                    return;
                }
                if (context.Request.Headers.TryGetValue("Origin", out var origins))
                {
                    string expected = $"http://{host.Host}:{host.Port}";
                    if (origins.Count != 1 || !string.Equals(origins[0], expected, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                    {
                        context.Response.StatusCode = 403;
                        await context.Response.WriteAsJsonAsync(new { error = "Cross-origin requests are not allowed" });
                        return;
                    }
                }
                context.Response.Headers.XContentTypeOptions = "nosniff";
                if (context.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments("/api")) context.Response.Headers.CacheControl = "no-store";
                await next();
            });
            app.UseRateLimiter();
            app.MapGet("/api/scenarios", (TrainingService service) => Results.Json(service.Scenarios()));
            // Shared by POST /api/test and POST /api/incident/answer: content type, 16 KiB body, JSON parsing and the 8-slot gate.
            async Task<IResult> ReadJsonBodyAsync(HttpContext context, Func<JsonElement, Task<IResult>> handle)
            {
                if (!System.Net.Http.Headers.MediaTypeHeaderValue.TryParse(context.Request.ContentType, out var type) || !string.Equals(type.MediaType, "application/json", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                    return Results.Json(new { error = "Content-Type must be application/json" }, statusCode: 415);
                if (context.Request.ContentLength is 0 or > 16384) return Results.Json(new { error = "Invalid request size" }, statusCode: 400);
                if (!await concurrentTests.WaitAsync(0, context.RequestAborted)) return Results.Json(new { error = "Too many concurrent tests" }, statusCode: 429);
                try
                {
                    using var buffer = new MemoryStream();
                    var bytes = new byte[4096];
                    while (true)
                    {
                        int count = await context.Request.Body.ReadAsync(bytes, context.RequestAborted);
                        if (count == 0) break;
                        if (buffer.Length + count > 16384) return Results.Json(new { error = "Invalid request size" }, statusCode: 400);
                        buffer.Write(bytes, 0, count);
                    }
                    if (buffer.Length == 0) return Results.Json(new { error = "Invalid request size" }, statusCode: 400);
                    using var document = JsonDocument.Parse(buffer.ToArray());
                    return await handle(document.RootElement);
                }
                catch (JsonException) { return Results.Json(new { error = "Invalid JSON" }, statusCode: 400); }
                catch (ArgumentException ex) { return Results.Json(new { error = ex.Message }, statusCode: 400); }
                finally { concurrentTests.Release(); }
            }
            app.MapPost("/api/test", (HttpContext context, TrainingService service) => ReadJsonBodyAsync(context, async payload =>
            {
                var request = TrainingService.Validate(payload);
                return Results.Json(await service.TestAsync(request, context.RequestAborted));
            }));
            app.MapGet("/api/incident/{scenario_id}/log", (string scenario_id, TrainingService service) =>
                service.IncidentLog(scenario_id) is { } log ? Results.Json(log) : Results.Json(new { error = "Not found" }, statusCode: 404));
            app.MapPost("/api/incident/answer", (HttpContext context, TrainingService service) => ReadJsonBodyAsync(context, async payload =>
            {
                var answer = TrainingService.ValidateAnswer(payload);
                return Results.Json(await service.AnswerAsync(answer, context.RequestAborted));
            }));
            app.Map("/api/{**path}", () => Results.Json(new { error = "Not found" }, statusCode: 404));
            var frontend = Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "frontend");
            if (!Directory.Exists(frontend)) throw new DirectoryNotFoundException($"Frontend assets not found: {frontend}");
            var files = new PhysicalFileProvider(frontend);
            app.UseDefaultFiles(new DefaultFilesOptions { FileProvider = files });
            app.UseStaticFiles(new StaticFileOptions { FileProvider = files });
            return app;
        }

        private static int PortFromEnvironment()
        {
            var value = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("GHOSTWIRE_PORT");
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(value)) return 8000;
            if (!int.TryParse(value, out int port) || port is < 1 or > 65535) throw new ArgumentException("GHOSTWIRE_PORT must be between 1 and 65535.");
            return port;
        }
    }
}

# Implementation Plan: ot-security-lab

Run the harness after every task from the repository root: `tools/dotnet run --project csharp/GhostWire.Tests/GhostWire.Tests.csproj`. A task is done only when the harness prints `All GhostWire protocol and HTTP checks passed.` No NuGet packages. No commits unless the owner asks.

  - Implement `Hex` (uppercase, space-separated).
  - Add example checks: the Giant Pressure request and response bytes from `modbus-protocol.md` decode to the expected fields; `84 02` decodes as exception 02.

- [x] 2.1 Add the seeded generator and runner to the harness

  - _Requirements: 4.3, 4.4, 1.6_
- [x] 2.3 Property P-b: decoder never throws on random byte arrays of length 0–300, in both directions (≥200 cases)

- [x] 3. Capture wire bytes on the client and the simulator
- [x] 3.1 Return exchanged bytes from `ModbusClient`
  - Add `ModbusExchange(Sent, Received)` to `ModbusResult`; set `Sent` only after the write completes; accumulate `Received` from the header and PDU reads.
  - Build the request with `ModbusCodec.EncodeReadRequest`.
  - Throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` before opening a socket when the function is not 3 or 4.
  - Add checks: a function-6 call throws and the simulator sees no exchange.
  - _Requirements: 1.3, 1.5, 5.3_

  - Record `(RemotePort, Received, Sent)` once per handled request; swallow recorder exceptions.
  - With `allowWrites: false` (default), FC06 still returns exception 01. With `allowWrites: true`, FC06 writes an existing holding register under a lock and echoes the request PDU; a missing address returns exception 02.

  - Move observations, causes, hints, next steps and `verified` from `TrainingService.TestAsync` into `Diagnosis.ForRead` with identical text for the three existing cases.

  - Script: 11 FC03 reads of register 100 by `HMI-01` (transaction IDs 1–11) and one FC06 write of 950 by `MAINT-LAPTOP-07` (transaction ID 1111) at sequence 8, with fixed simulated timestamps.

# Judge quick start

1. From the project root, run `dotnet run --project csharp/GhostWire/GhostWire.csproj` with the .NET 8 SDK. Alternatively, unzip the Windows release package, which requires the .NET 8 ASP.NET Core Runtime (x64), and run `GhostWire.exe`.
2. Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. No login, physical PLC, sensor or AI key is required for the core simulation. The case picker groups **Troubleshooting** and **Security incidents** and shows each case's difficulty.
3. Select **The Giant Pressure** and run the read. Inspect raw 39 and the simulated documentation. Set the scale to 0.01 and retest: the displayed result is 0.39 bar.
4. Open **Wire evidence (simulated frames)** under the verification line. The request is `00 01 00 00 00 06 07 03 00 0A 00 01` and the response is `00 01 00 00 00 05 07 03 02 00 27`. Tab to a field row, or hover it, to highlight its bytes; the row also states the byte range in text (for example "bytes 0–1" for the transaction ID). The panel defines MBAP header, PDU, unit ID and function code. Wire evidence is available after every read in every case, including Phantom Writer's initial read.
5. Select **The Silent Sensor**, run the initial read, inspect the timeout and possible causes. Wire evidence shows only the request frame (`00 01 00 00 00 06 01 04 00 00 00 01`) because no response arrived. Check the simulated documentation, set Unit ID to 17 and retest: the simulator returns raw 73 and the read is verified. The timeout alone did not prove the unit ID was the cause; the successful retest with 17 is what verifies the setting.
6. Select **The Wrong Register**, run the read and open Wire evidence: the response `00 01 00 00 00 03 03 84 02` decodes as function `84 · Exception for 04` and exception code `02 · Illegal Data Address`. Compare address 21 to the simulated zero-based map at 20, then retest with 20: the simulator returns raw 125 and the read is verified.
7. Select **Phantom Writer** (security, intermediate) and run the initial read (unit 5, function 03, address 100, quantity 1, scale 0.1). The simulator returns raw 950, shown as 95 °C, while the simulated documentation states a normal setpoint of 650 (65.0 °C). The read verifies the current simulated setpoint, not who changed it.
8. In **Simulated traffic log**, review the 12 captured transactions. Identify the entry that changed the setpoint: its simulated time, client label, transaction ID, unit ID, register and old and new value. Expand **Frames** on a row to see its bytes. Press **Select** on the row to copy its transaction ID and client label into the answer form, then **Submit answer**.
9. Expected verified outcome: transaction 1111 at 2026-10-31T02:13:33Z from client label MAINT-LAPTOP-07 is function 06 (Write Single Register) to unit 5, register 100, value 950; the last read before it (transaction 7) returned 650 and the next read (transaction 8) returned 950. The row is then marked "⚠ Unauthorized write", and four mitigations appear under "Next steps · real-world guidance, not verified by this simulation". A wrong pair returns "not verified" without revealing the correct one.
10. Inspect observations, hypotheses, training hints, verification and case history (reads and answer attempts). The report can be printed via the browser.

All devices and measurements are simulated. The server is limited to loopback; it cannot test or write real equipment. Learners cannot send Modbus writes; the Phantom Writer FC06 happens only inside the server's private simulator at startup. Modbus TCP frames carry no client identity, so client labels are capture metadata. Mitigations are guidance and are not verified by this simulation. Timeout is not proof of a particular cause. External AI is optional and may be wrong.

content.oldText:
# Judge quick start

1. From the project root, run `dotnet run --project csharp/GhostWire/GhostWire.csproj` with the .NET 8 SDK. Alternatively, unzip the Windows release package, which requires the .NET 8 ASP.NET Core Runtime (x64), and run `GhostWire.exe`.
2. Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. No login, physical PLC, sensor or AI key is required for the core simulation. The case picker groups **Troubleshooting** and **Security incidents** and shows each case's difficulty.
3. Select **The Giant Pressure** and run the read. Inspect raw 39 and the simulated documentation. Set the scale to 0.01 and retest: the displayed result is 0.39 bar.
4. Open **Wire evidence (simulated frames)** under the verification line. The request is `00 01 00 00 00 06 07 03 00 0A 00 01` and the response is `00 01 00 00 00 05 07 03 02 00 27`. Tab to a field row, or hover it, to highlight its bytes; the row also states the byte range in text (for example "bytes 0–1" for the transaction ID). The panel defines MBAP header, PDU, unit ID and function code. Wire evidence is available after every read in every case, including Phantom Writer's initial read.
5. Select **The Silent Sensor**, run the initial read, inspect the timeout and possible causes. Wire evidence shows only the request frame (`00 01 00 00 00 06 01 04 00 00 00 01`) because no response arrived. Check the simulated documentation, set Unit ID to 17 and retest: the simulator returns raw 73 and the read is verified. The timeout alone did not prove the unit ID was the cause; the successful retest with 17 is what verifies the setting.
6. Select **The Wrong Register**, run the read and open Wire evidence: the response `00 01 00 00 00 03 03 84 02` decodes as function `84 · Exception for 04` and exception code `02 · Illegal Data Address`. Compare address 21 to the simulated zero-based map at 20, then retest with 20: the simulator returns raw 125 and the read is verified.
7. Select **Phantom Writer** (security, intermediate) and run the initial read (unit 5, function 03, address 100, quantity 1, scale 0.1). The simulator returns raw 950, shown as 95 °C, while the simulated documentation states a normal setpoint of 650 (65.0 °C). The read verifies the current simulated setpoint, not who changed it.
8. In **Simulated traffic log**, review the 12 captured transactions. Identify the entry that changed the setpoint: its simulated time, client label, transaction ID, unit ID, register and old and new value. Expand **Frames** on a row to see its bytes. Press **Select** on the row to copy its transaction ID and client label into the answer form, then **Submit answer**.
9. Expected verified outcome: transaction 1111 at 2026-10-31T02:13:33Z from client label MAINT-LAPTOP-07 is function 06 (Write Single Register) to unit 5, register 100, value 950; the last read before it (transaction 7) returned 650 and the next read (transaction 8) returned 950. The row is then marked "⚠ Unauthorized write", and four mitigations appear under "Next steps · real-world guidance, not verified by this simulation". A wrong pair returns "not verified" without revealing the correct one.
10. Inspect observations, hypotheses, training hints, verification and case history (reads and answer attempts). The report can be printed via the browser.

All devices and measurements are simulated. The server is limited to loopback; it cannot test or write real equipment. Learners cannot send Modbus writes; the Phantom Writer FC06 happens only inside the server's private simulator at startup. Modbus TCP frames carry no client identity, so client labels are capture metadata. Mitigations are guidance and are not verified by this simulation. Timeout is not proof of a particular cause. External AI is optional and may be wrong.

The timeout alone did not prove the unit ID was the cause; the successful retest with 17 is what verifies the setting.

## ot-security-lab feature (frame inspector, Phantom Writer, categories, property tests), 2026-11-11

Observed in the local WSL environment using Windows .NET SDK 8.0.427 through `tools/dotnet`.

- `tools/dotnet build csharp/GhostWire/GhostWire.csproj` succeeded with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- `tools/dotnet run --project csharp/GhostWire.Tests/GhostWire.Tests.csproj` printed `PBT seed: 1616322598 (0x60572026) (default)`, `Check calls passed: 26671` and `All GhostWire protocol and HTTP checks passed.` on two consecutive runs. Property results, with the elapsed time from one run:
  - P-a codec round-trip (FC03/FC04/FC06 requests and responses, exceptions): 600 cases, 14 ms.
  - P-b decoder never throws on 0–300 random bytes, both directions: 600 cases, 13 ms.
  - P-e frames hex equals the bytes the simulator recorded: 200 cases, 4,585 ms.
  - P-c transport status partition (response/exception/timeout, register count equals quantity, exception 02 out of map): 200 cases in batches of 8, 4,844 ms.
  - P-d timeout diagnosis is never verified, has at least two causes, at least one not about the unit ID, and no certainty wording: 400 cases, 16 ms.
- One run with `GHOSTWIRE_PBT_SEED=12345` also passed and printed `PBT seed used: 12345`.
- Example checks that passed in the same run include: the Giant Pressure request `00 01 00 00 00 06 07 03 00 0A 00 01` and response `00 01 00 00 00 05 07 03 02 00 27` (field `Register 10 = 39 (0x0027)`); the Silent Sensor timeout returns one request frame; the Wrong Register response decodes `02 · Illegal Data Address`; `ModbusClient` refuses function 6 before any bytes reach the simulator; the default simulator answers FC06 with `86 01` and leaves the register unchanged; the learner-facing `phantom-writer` simulator answers FC06 with `86 01` and register 100 still reads 950; the Phantom Writer read returns raw 950, 95 °C, `verified: true`; four scenarios with the specified categories and difficulties.
- Traffic log checks: 12 entries, unique transaction IDs, exactly one FC06 entry, two client labels, every frame re-decodes to its entry's fields, and identical JSON from two independent `TrainingService` instances. `/api/incident/unit-id/log`, `/api/incident/../log` and an encoded traversal id return 404.
- Answer checks: transaction 1111 with `MAINT-LAPTOP-07` verifies with four labeled mitigations and observations citing function 06, unit 5, register 100, 650, 950, `2026-10-31T02:13:33Z` and the label. A wrong client, a read transaction and a missing transaction each return `verified: false`, no mitigations and no `MAINT-LAPTOP-07` in the body. Extra, duplicate and missing fields, a non-security scenario, `transaction_id` 70000 or as a string, client `a b`, a 33-character client and invalid JSON return 400; `text/plain` returns 415; a foreign Origin or Host returns 403; an oversized body is rejected.
- Local test provider: the provider request contains `frames` (and `log_entry` for answers); provider text left `verified`, `frames` and `mitigations` unchanged for `/api/test` and `/api/incident/answer`. This is not an external AI-provider test.
- Traffic log served by the running server (`GET /api/incident/phantom-writer/log`): sequences 1–7 are FC03 reads by `HMI-01`, transactions 1–7, at 02:13:00Z to 02:13:30Z, each returning 650 (`… 05 03 02 02 8A`). Sequence 8 is FC06 by `MAINT-LAPTOP-07`, transaction 1111, at 02:13:33Z: request and echo `04 57 00 00 00 06 05 06 00 64 03 B6`. Sequences 9–12 are FC03 reads by `HMI-01`, transactions 8–11, at 02:13:35Z to 02:13:50Z, each returning 950 (`… 05 03 02 03 B6`).

### Browser checks (Windows Chrome headless driven over the DevTools protocol by a temporary script outside the repository)

35 of 35 checks passed against the running server after one fix (the answer button no longer becomes `disabled` during submission, which had dropped keyboard focus):

- The picker shows "Troubleshooting" and "Security incidents" groups with difficulty in the option text; the traffic log panel is hidden for troubleshooting cases and shown for Phantom Writer.
- Keyboard only: Tab reached the Wire evidence summary, Enter opened it, and Tab moved through field rows. Each focused row highlighted its bytes (underline as well as background) and stated "bytes 0–1", "byte 6" and so on as text. Tab reached a log row's Select button, Enter filled the answer form, and the flagged row was reachable with Tab. Focus stayed on the submit button while the result was announced in the `role="status"` message.
- No row was marked before a verified answer. After the verified answer the FC06 row showed "⚠ Unauthorized write" with a double left border and hatched background, and four mitigations under "Next steps · real-world guidance, not verified by this simulation". A wrong answer showed "Status: answer not verified" and no mitigations.
- Emulated `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` set the byte-highlight transition to 0s.
- Emulated print media hid the investigation panels, kept case history, expanded the answer attempts, and `Page.printToPDF` rendered.

Not checked: a screen reader, a real mobile device, a physical printer, startup failure injection for the incident generator (the code throws and the host resolves the service eagerly, but no harness check forces a mismatch), and the empty `frames` case for a request that was never written (not reproducible on a working loopback listener).

### Security review

The `ot-security-reviewer` agent reviewed commit 0b62fab against `safety.md` (session `sess_6771b137-8663-47a2-b2ec-149419fbbada`, see `docs/kiro-log/LEDGER.md`). It reported 0 critical, 0 high and 0 medium findings, 3 low findings and 2 info findings.

- Low, `Modbus.cs` header mismatch: fixed in code. When the response header fails validation, `ModbusClient` keeps the 7 header bytes it received and the response frame's `decode_error` now reads, for example, `Client stopped after header: transaction ID mismatch. Only the 7 header bytes received were kept.` Before the fix, the decoder reported a "Truncated frame" error, which made it look as if the simulator had sent a short frame. A new harness check uses a loopback fake server that replies with transaction ID 2 and asserts that error text and the received bytes `00 02 00 00 00 05 07`.
- Low, `docs/video/storyboard.md` opening line: the narration now starts "In this simulation", and the shot description names the on-screen text "Status: response" instead of a color change.
- Low, `docs/video/storyboard.md` Phantom Writer line: the narration now says "then see real-world guidance that this simulation does not verify".
- The two info findings (learner `client` text in the AI prompt, `DisposeAsync` not awaiting in-flight handlers) were not changed.

After the fix, `tools/dotnet run --project csharp/GhostWire.Tests/GhostWire.Tests.csproj` printed `PBT seed used: 1616322598`, `Check calls passed: 26672` and `All GhostWire protocol and HTTP checks passed.` It ran with `-p:BaseOutputPath` set to a Windows temp folder because a running `GhostWire.exe` held a lock on the default `bin` output.

## Windows x64 executable package, 2026-11-10

- Published with Windows .NET SDK 8.0.427 using `dotnet publish -c Release --no-restore --self-contained false`. The apphost is a 148 KiB PE32+ executable; the full folder occupied 264 KiB before adding its README. Runtime dependencies are not bundled.
- Launched the published `GhostWire.exe` on the same machine with .NET 8 runtimes installed. It listened on Windows loopback. HTTP calls through Windows Node verified pressure correction to 0.39, silent-sensor timeout then verified response, wrong-register exception then verified response, and deterministic fallback.
- The executable was not tested on a separate machine or without the required .NET 8 ASP.NET Core Runtime.

- Windows .NET SDK 8.0.427: `dotnet build csharp/GhostWire/GhostWire.csproj` succeeded with zero warnings and errors.
- `dotnet run --project csharp/GhostWire.Tests/GhostWire.Tests.csproj` reported all protocol and HTTP checks passed, including loopback TCP reads, three scenarios, invalid input, host/origin and body limits, rate limiting, a local test provider and fallback. This is not an external AI-provider test.

- Not tested: physical devices, Modbus interoperability with an independent implementation, external AI provider, public deployment, or genuine Kiro development use. C# source has not yet been published to GitHub.

## Historical Python implementation

Historical Python implementation, observed 2026-11-10 in the local WSL environment. These results do not establish the behavior of the C# replacement:

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s backend/tests -v`: 11 tests passed. These include real loopback TCP simulator/client reads, FC03 and FC04, address exception, simulated unit mismatch timeout, write rejection, API validation and local-provider/fallback tests. Provider tests use a local test service; they do not establish a successful external AI-provider call.
- Browser against the local server: Giant Pressure changed from 39 bar, not verified, to 0.39 bar, verified, after scale 0.01. Silent Sensor timed out at Unit ID 1 and returned a verified response at 17. Wrong Register returned exception 02 at address 21 and verified at 20. The explanation was labeled deterministic fallback.
- Mobile browser inspection reported document width and scroll width both 360 CSS pixels at the sampled viewport; no browser error entries were reported during the inspected session. This is not a full accessibility or cross-browser audit.
- Not tested: physical PLCs or sensors, external AI provider, deployment, independent Modbus implementation interoperability, end-to-end Kiro usage, or a public repository.

These are simulator and local software checks only, not safety certification or evidence about physical equipment.

- The picker shows "Troubleshooting" and "Security incidents" groups with difficulty in the option text; the traffic log panel is hidden for troubleshooting cases and shown for Phantom Writer.
- Keyboard only: Tab reached the Wire evidence summary, Enter opened it, and Tab moved through field rows. Each focused row highlighted its bytes (underline as well as background) and stated "bytes 0–1", "byte 6" and so on as text. Tab reached a log row's Select button, Enter filled the answer form, and the flagged row was reachable with Tab. Focus stayed on the submit button while the result was announced in the `role="status"` message.
- No row was marked before a verified answer. After the verified answer the FC06 row showed "⚠ Unauthorized write" with a double left border and hatched background, and four mitigations under "Next steps · real-world guidance, not verified by this simulation". A wrong answer showed "Status: answer not verified" and no mitigations.
- Emulated `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` set the byte-highlight transition to 0s.
- Emulated print media hid the investigation panels, kept case history, expanded the answer attempts, and `Page.printToPDF` rendered.

Not checked: a screen reader, a real mobile device, a physical printer, startup failure injection for the incident generator (the code throws and the host resolves the service eagerly, but no harness check forces a mismatch), and the empty `frames` case for a request that was never written (not reproducible on a working loopback listener).

### Security review

The `ot-security-reviewer` agent reviewed commit 0b62fab against `safety.md` (session `sess_6771b137-8663-47a2-b2ec-149419fbbada`, see `docs/kiro-log/LEDGER.md`). It reported 0 critical, 0 high and 0 medium findings, 3 low findings and 2 info findings.

- Low, `Modbus.cs` header mismatch: fixed in code. When the response header fails validation, `ModbusClient` keeps the 7 header bytes it received and the response frame's `decode_error` now reads, for example, `Client stopped after header: transaction ID mismatch. Only the 7 header bytes received were kept.` Before the fix, the decoder reported a "Truncated frame" error, which made it look as if the simulator had sent a short frame. A new harness check uses a loopback fake server that replies with transaction ID 2 and asserts that error text and the received bytes `00 02 00 00 00 05 07`.
- Low, `docs/video/storyboard.md` opening line: the narration now starts "In this simulation", and the shot description names the on-screen text "Status: response" instead of a color change.
- Low, `docs/video/storyboard.md` Phantom Writer line: the narration now says "then see real-world guidance that this simulation does not verify".
- The two info findings (learner `client` text in the AI prompt, `DisposeAsync` not awaiting in-flight handlers) were not changed.

After the fix, `tools/dotnet run --project csharp/GhostWire.Tests/GhostWire.Tests.csproj` printed `PBT seed used: 1616322598`, `Check calls passed: 26672` and `All GhostWire protocol and HTTP checks passed.` It ran with `-p:BaseOutputPath` set to a Windows temp folder because a running `GhostWire.exe` held a lock on the default `bin` output.

## Windows x64 executable package, 2026-11-10

- Published with Windows .NET SDK 8.0.427 using `dotnet publish -c Release --no-restore --self-contained false`. The apphost is a 148 KiB PE32+ executable; the full folder occupied 264 KiB before adding its README. Runtime dependencies are not bundled.
- Launched the published `GhostWire.exe` on the same machine with .NET 8 runtimes installed. It listened on Windows loopback. HTTP calls through Windows Node verified pressure correction to 0.39, silent-sensor timeout then verified response, wrong-register exception then verified response, and deterministic fallback.
- The executable was not tested on a separate machine or without the required .NET 8 ASP.NET Core Runtime.

## C# implementation, 2026-11-10

- Windows .NET SDK 8.0.427: `dotnet build csharp/GhostWire/GhostWire.csproj` succeeded with zero warnings and errors.
- `dotnet run --project csharp/GhostWire.Tests/GhostWire.Tests.csproj` reported all protocol and HTTP checks passed, including loopback TCP reads, three scenarios, invalid input, host/origin and body limits, rate limiting, a local test provider and fallback. This is not an external AI-provider test.
- Windows Chrome headless exercised three fault-and-retest flows against the running C# server: 0.39 bar for corrected pressure; silent sensor timeout then verified response; wrong address exception then verified response. Case switching restored two actual pressure reads, comparison showed the changed scale, and the print button became enabled. A 320-CSS-pixel viewport reported no horizontal overflow. `docs/csharp-desktop-check.png` is an observed Windows Chrome screenshot.
- Color measurements for three representative text/background pairs passed 4.5:1. This is not a full accessibility audit, a screen-reader test, or a real-device mobile test.
- Not tested: physical devices, Modbus interoperability with an independent implementation, external AI provider, public deployment, or genuine Kiro development use. C# source has not yet been published to GitHub.

## Historical Python implementation

Historical Python implementation, observed 2026-11-10 in the local WSL environment. These results do not establish the behavior of the C# replacement:

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s backend/tests -v`: 11 tests passed. These include real loopback TCP simulator/client reads, FC03 and FC04, address exception, simulated unit mismatch timeout, write rejection, API validation and local-provider/fallback tests. Provider tests use a local test service; they do not establish a successful external AI-provider call.
- Browser against the local server: Giant Pressure changed from 39 bar, not verified, to 0.39 bar, verified, after scale 0.01. Silent Sensor timed out at Unit ID 1 and returned a verified response at 17. Wrong Register returned exception 02 at address 21 and verified at 20. The explanation was labeled deterministic fallback.
- Mobile browser inspection reported document width and scroll width both 360 CSS pixels at the sampled viewport; no browser error entries were reported during the inspected session. This is not a full accessibility or cross-browser audit.
- Not tested: physical PLCs or sensors, external AI provider, deployment, independent Modbus implementation interoperability, end-to-end Kiro usage, or a public repository.

These are simulator and local software checks only, not safety certification or evidence about physical equipment.

I'll start by reading the spec, frontend files, and relevant C# code.
Now I have the full picture. Making the edits, starting with the favicon file.
Now the JavaScript: request validation first.
Now the traffic log rows, hints, and tour.
I accidentally added a duplicate Seq cell; removing it.
Now the hint logic in `showIncident` and the answer submit handler.
Now the CSS.
Running the syntax check and the test harness.
Tests pass. Now the headless Chrome check. I'll start the server on a separate port and write a temporary CDP script to the Windows temp folder.
Removing a placeholder check that would always pass, then running the script.
All 28 checks pass. The new server log shows no "Application started", so I'll confirm which server answered and that it served the updated CSS.
The leftover processes are the test server I started (`GhostWire.exe` on port 8765 and its `dotnet run` parent). Stopping them, then cleaning up the temporary script folder.
Now the docs and the spec task list.
Final harness run after the CSS fix, plus a status check.
`docs/devpost-draft.md` shows as modified, but I didn't edit it. Checking what changed.
All five fixes are in and the test harness passes. A headless Windows Chrome run passed 28 of 28 checks, covering everything you listed. No server code changed and nothing is committed.

## What changed

**`frontend/index.html`**, **`frontend/app.js`** and **`frontend/styles.css`**, by issue:

1. **Phantom Writer answers**
   - The per-row "Select" buttons and the "Answer" column are gone, so the learner has to type the transaction ID and client label.
   - Each row still has one keyboard stop: a "Show frames" toggle. It opens that row's frames in a full-width row underneath instead of a narrow cell. The marked FC06 row is still focusable after a correct answer.
   - The hints are client-side, since the server doesn't count wrong answers. They appear under the answer form in a "Training hints" box, labeled "Specific to this simulated case", and are also announced in the status message.
   - I read "progressive" as: hint 1 after the 3rd wrong answer, hint 2 added after the 4th. Both hide once an answer is verified, and neither names the row. Say if you want a different schedule.

2. **Favicon:** new `frontend/favicon.svg` (a ghost above a green wire line, in the theme colors), linked from `index.html` and served by the existing static handler.

3. **Invalid inputs**
   - The read form now checks unit ID, address, quantity, scale and address + quantity against the server's limits before sending anything.
   - On the first bad field it sends nothing, sets `aria-invalid`, focuses the field and shows a message such as "Unit ID must be a whole number from 1 to 247. Nothing was sent."
   - The scale field now also has `max="1000000"` to match the server.

4. **Log layout**
   - Times show as HH:MM:SS. The full ISO timestamp is in a tooltip and in hidden text for screen readers, and the caption says "times in UTC".
   - Cells no longer wrap, except the Function column.
   - On narrow screens the table scrolls sideways inside a labeled, focusable region, with a "Scroll the table sideways" note that is hidden on wide screens.
   - The FC06 row is still marked only after a correct answer.

5. **Guided tour:** a dismissible banner that appears once the cases have loaded. Its button selects The Silent Sensor and focuses the case picker. Dismissal is saved in localStorage. The banner has no animation, so reduced motion has nothing to turn off.

**Docs and spec**
- `docs/judge-quick-start.md`: Phantom Writer step 8 now says to type the answer, describes the hints, "Show frames" and the short times. Step 2 mentions the tour and the "Nothing was sent" message.
- `.kiro/specs/ot-security-lab/tasks.md`: added task 15 (done) and noted on task 12 that "Select" was removed.
- `docs/verification.md`: added a section with the results below.

## Results

- **Test harness:** `tools/dotnet run --project csharp/GhostWire.Tests/GhostWire.Tests.csproj` printed `All GhostWire protocol and HTTP checks passed.` (seed 1616322598).
- **Chrome checks (Chrome 157, port 8765):**
  - `/favicon.svg` returned 200, and the run had no 4xx/5xx responses and no console errors or warnings.
  - The log has no Select buttons.
  - Hint 1 appears after the 3rd wrong answer and hint 2 after the 4th. Wrong answers revealed nothing, and typing `1111` / `MAINT-LAPTOP-07` verified.
  - Unit 999 sent no request and showed the message. Address 70000, quantity 0 and scale 0 were also blocked.
  - At 360 px the page was 360 px wide, with no sideways scroll, even with frames open.
  - The tour button selects The Silent Sensor, and dismissal survives a reload.

The first Chrome run found a real bug at 360 px: the page grew to 1000 px wide. Hidden text inside the scrolling table was escaping it. Adding `position: relative` to the scroll container fixed it, and the run above is after that fix.

The temporary script and Chrome profiles in the Windows temp folder are deleted, and the test server is stopped.

## Open items

- `docs/devpost-draft.md` changed during this session, but not by me: the release URL was filled in. I left it alone.
- Not checked: a real screen reader, print preview, and browsers other than Chrome.
